land.text: Gauda and Bengal, which fell to Sher Shah in April 1538; Sher Shah already ruled Bihar ('Sultan of Bihar' 1530 - 6 April 1538)

predecessors.note: The sultanate-of-bengal dossier (sa-04-c) ends on 6 April 1538 with the Hussain Shahi line and names sur-empire as successor. Cliopatria's separate 'Hussain Shahi Dynasty' row (1534-1539) is the same Bengal; see the hussain-shahi-dynasty dossier.

land.text: Orissa as Cliopatria draws it from 1579: the coastal plain round Cuttack, Puri and Balasore

successors.note: At the end (1593) only Orissa was left, taken by Man Singh for Akbar. Earlier handovers to the same successor: the Punjab and Delhi in 1555, Delhi and Agra in November 1556, Patna in 1574 and Bengal in 1576 (all in the ledger). Cliopatria's Mughal shape takes Orissa only in 1595; the mughal-empire dossier dates it 1595 at confidence 1.

capitals.name: Sasaram
capitals.note: The Sur Empire infobox lists 'Sasaram Delhi' as capitals and the text calls Sasaram the capital 'in modern-day Bihar'; no page dates the years, so 1538-1539 (before Kannauj) is my reading.

capitals.name: Delhi
capitals.note: Sher Shah Suri page: 'he declared Delhi his seat of power' (undated); taken here from his Hindustan title of 17 May 1540 to the Mughal occupation of Delhi in 1555. The Panipat page has Hemu crowned at Purana Quila in Delhi in October 1556.

capitals.name: Gaur (Gauda)
capitals.note: Karrani page: Taj Khan's seat was Gaur. The pages opened do not name the seat of the Muhammad Shahi dynasty (1553-1563), so Gaur for 1556-1563 is my reading.

capitals.name: Tanda
capitals.note: Karrani page: Sulaiman Khan moved the capital to Tanda in 1565; Munim Khan captured Tanda on 25 September 1574. Coordinates are approximate (Tanda is not in the gazetteer).

capitals.name: Cuttack (Katak)
capitals.note: Daud submitted at Cuttack on 12 April 1575 and kept only Orissa; no page opened names the seat of the Afghans of Orissa, so Cuttack is my reading.

rulers.name: Sher Shah Suri
rulers.note: Sur Empire table: '6 April 1538/17 May 1540 to 22 May 1545'; died at Kalinjar.

rulers.name: Sikandar Shah Suri
rulers.note: February to 22 June 1555 (Sirhind); he surrendered to Bairam Khan on 25 July 1557.

rulers.name: Adil Shah Suri
rulers.note: 22 June 1555 to 1556; the Second Battle of Panipat page has him defeated and killed by Khizr Khan of Bengal in April 1557. The Muhammad Shahi dynasty of Bengal (1553-1563) has no ruler list on the pages opened, so the strip has a gap 1557-1563.

rulers.name: Dawud Khan Karrani
rulers.note: Executed after Rajmahal (1576). The pages opened give no rulers for Orissa 1576-1593 (Qutlu Khan, then his son Nasir Khan, are named by the Mughal conquest page without dates).

correction.text: 'Sultan of Bengal and Bihar': Bihar, held by Sher Shah since 1530, and the Bengal taken at Gauda in April 1538

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1538-1539: Cliopatria's Sur row begins in 1540, but the Sher Shah Suri page gives 'Sultan of Bengal and Bihar, 6 April 1538 - 17 May 1540' and Gauda fell in April 1538. Humayun held Gauda from 8 September 1538 (Sur Empire page), which the ledger carries as a contest. No area on the page.

correction.text: the 1540 shape plus the Punjab of Pakistan with Lahore (captured November 1540) and Multan (1541)

keyframe_review.note: 865,421 km2 for 1540-1546 holds Hindustan (Delhi, Agra, the Doab, Bihar, Bengal) and part of Malwa and Rajasthan, but no Pakistan at all (0 cells of the Punjab). The Sur Empire page has the Punjab and Lahore captured in November 1540 and Multan in 1541, so the Punjab belongs from 1540-1541; Malwa (1542) and Marwar (1544-1545) are in the ledger. The page has no area, so the 1.25 M km2 of the 1547 shape cannot be compared.

1.25 M km2 (the Punjab of Pakistan, Multan, Malwa, Rajasthan now inside). The Sher Shah Suri page says the empire at his death 'spanned nearly the entirety of Northern India' and excluded Assam, Kashmir, Gujarat and the North-West Frontier Province; the shape holds 128 cells (32,000 km2, 3 percent) of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which is below the precision of the era, so it stands. Upper Sindh as far as Sehwan (page: undated, after the 1543 campaign) is mostly outside the shape (13 Sind cells). No infobox area to compare.

correction.text: the 1552 shape with Malwa restored until Baz Bahadur's independence in 1555

keyframe_review.note: The shape loses 159 cells of Madhya Pradesh (Malwa) and 27 of Rajasthan in 1552. The Sur Empire page annexes Malwa in 1542 and gives no loss before Islam Shah's death in 1554; the malwa-sultanate dossier (a page not opened here) dates Baz Bahadur's independence to 1555. Malwa is therefore kept until 1555. Bengal is drawn as Sur although the page lists the Muhammad Shahi dynasty from 1553; the ledger's renames carry the dynasties. The Punjab and Delhi go in 1555 (Sirhind).

1.22 M to 331,702 km2: the Punjab and Delhi are gone (Sirhind, June 1555), Delhi and Agra after Panipat (5 November 1556), and the shape is the east: Bihar, Jharkhand, Bengal and the north of Orissa. The Sur Empire page lists the Muhammad Shahi dynasty of Bengal 1553-1563 and the Panipat page has Adil Shah killed by Khizr Khan of Bengal in April 1557, so this is the Afghan sultanate of Bengal, kept under this dossier by Cliopatria's row and by the mughal-empire dossier's counterpart. What happened to the Sur land east of Agra (Jaunpur, Chunar) in 1556-1563 is not on the pages opened. No area on the page.

331,194 km2, almost the 1556 shape: the Karrani page has Taj Khan 'captured south-eastern Bihar and West Bengal' and then 'seized all of Bengal' in 1564. Sulaiman's authority was 'from Koch Bihar to Puri, and from Son River to Brahmaputra River'. No infobox area.

correction.text: the shape unchanged, for 1572-1573 only (Bengal, Bihar and Orissa under Daud Khan Karrani); later years are the new keyframes

keyframe_review.note: 369,294 km2: Cliopatria adds Orissa in 1572 (205 Odisha cells), four years after the Karrani page's 'In 1568, Sulaiman Khan annexed Orissa'. The shape is right for 1572-1573 only; Patna goes in August 1574 and Tanda in September 1574, so the new keyframe sur-empire_1574 replaces it from 1574 and sur-empire_1577 from 1577.

correction.text: the 1572 shape without Patna and Hajipur, lost in August 1574; Bengal still Daud's until Rajmahal

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1574-1576: Cliopatria keeps the whole 1572 shape to 1578. The Mughal conquest page has the siege of Patna from 3 August 1574, Tanda entered on 25 September 1574, Tukaroi in 1575 and Daud's submission at Cuttack on 12 April 1575; Bengal stays Daud's in fact until Rajmahal (10 July 1576). Patna and Hajipur are taken out; Bengal is contested in the ledger.

correction.text: Orissa alone, the Afghans' last land after Rajmahal

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1577-1578: after Rajmahal (July 1576) Bengal is Mughal and the Afghans hold only Orissa ('Daud ceded Bengal and Bihar and kept only Orissa', Karrani page); Cliopatria draws this shape from 1579.

38,835 km2, the coastal part of Orissa (117 Odisha cells of about 570); Daud rose again in Orissa and captured Bhadrak and Jaleswar (undated on the page), Qutlu Khan's son Nasir Khan ruled Odisha in 1590. A fraction of the 143,000 km2 of modern Odisha, but the pages give no boundary.

correction.text: the shape unchanged, for 1588-1593 (the Afghans of Orissa until Man Singh's conquest)

keyframe_review.note: The shape is unchanged to 1594, but the Mughal conquest page has Man Singh winning near the Subarnarekha in April 1592 and conquering Odisha 'the following year', returning to Bihar in 1593. The shape holds 1588-1592; 1593 is the conquest year and the state ends in it (the mughal-empire dossier dates the Mughal gain 1595 at confidence 1).

region.text: Bihar and Bengal, the lands of Sher Shah's titles

ledger.note: 1538: Sher Shah Suri takes Gauda and is crowned Sultan of Bengal and Bihar. 'Sher Shah besieged Gauda, which fell in April 1538'; infobox reign line: Sultan of Bengal and Bihar from 6 April 1538 to 17 May 1540. The Sur Empire page's own span is 1538/1540 to 1556.

region.text: the line of the war from Gauda in Bengal through Chausa in Bihar to Kannauj in the Doab

ledger.note: September 1538: Humayun seizes Gauda. The Sur Empire page has Humayun mobilizing in July 1537, reaching Chunar that November and seizing Gauda on 8 September 1538; the war runs through Chausa (June 1539 per the Sher Shah infobox 'Chausa (1539)'; the Sur page gives no date) to Kannauj. The mughal-empire dossier opens its contest at Chausa, June 1539.

region.text: the line of the war from Gauda in Bengal through Chausa in Bihar to Kannauj in the Doab

ledger.note: 17 May 1540: Sher Shah routs Humayun at Kannauj and ends the war. Sur Empire infobox: Battle of Kannauj, 17 May 1540; after Kannauj Humayun fled to Sindh.

region.text: Hindustan: Humayun's Delhi, Agra and the Ganges-Yamuna Doab

ledger.note: 17 May 1540: Sher Shah becomes Sultan of Hindustan. Infobox reign line: Sultan of Hindustan from 17 May 1540 to 22 May 1545; he 'was crowned a second time on 17 May 1540' and declared Delhi his seat. The page names no boundary; Delhi, Agra and the Doab are my reading of Hindustan.

region.text: the Punjab with Lahore

ledger.note: November 1540: the Punjab falls to the Afghans. The Sur Empire page has Punjab and Lahore captured in November 1540; the Sher Shah Suri page has Humayun at Lahore in July 1540 with the Afghans at Sultanpur Lodhi and 50,000 men stationed in the Punjab, and the mughal-empire dossier dates the Mughal loss to July 1540.

region.text: Multan

ledger.counterpart: Multan (holder not named on the page)
ledger.note: 1541: the Afghans take Multan. Sur Empire page: 'After conquering Multan in 1541, it was later overrun by Baloch tribes'; Sher Shah assembled for a campaign in 1543. The page names no previous holder.

region.text: Malwa, with Gwalior

ledger.note: 1542: Sher Shah annexes Malwa. 'In 1542, Sher Shah embarked on a campaign to Malwa', and Malwa was annexed; the Sur Empire page adds that Gwalior was subjugated. The siege of Raisen (1542-1543 in the infobox) is not dated on the Sur page. The malwa-sultanate dossier records the same loss in 1542.

region.text: upper Sindh as far as Sehwan

ledger.counterpart: Upper Sindh (rulers not named on the page)
ledger.note: Undated, placed 1544: Haibat Khan subjugates upper Sindh. Sur Empire page: after the 1543 campaign against Fateh Khan Jat, 'Haibat Khan would subjugate upper Sindh as far as Sehwan'. The page gives no year, only 'following the campaign' in Sher Shah's reign (to May 1545); the year is a bridge. Cliopatria's 1547 shape has only 13 Sind cells.

region.text: Marwar from Ajmer to Mount Abu

ledger.note: 1544: Sher Shah's generals occupy Marwar. After the campaign of 'early 1543' against Maldeo Rathore and the battle of Sammel, in 1544 Khawas Khan took Jodhpur and occupied Marwar from Ajmer to Mount Abu. The kingdom-of-marwar dossier records the same occupation.

region.text: Marwar from Ajmer to Mount Abu

ledger.note: July 1545: Maldeo retakes Marwar. Sur Empire page: Maldeo recaptured Jodhpur 'by July 1545' and his territories 'by 1546'; Sher Shah died at Kalinjar on 22 May 1545 (Sher Shah Suri page).

region.text: Malwa

ledger.note: 1555: Malwa slips away. The Sur Empire page is silent after the 1542 annexation; the malwa-sultanate dossier dates Baz Bahadur's independence to 1555 (a page not opened here). Cliopatria's shape drops Malwa in 1552.

region.text: the Punjab from Lahore to Sirhind and the country round Delhi

ledger.note: February 1555: the Mughals take Lahore and Rohtas Fort, opening the reconquest. Sirhind page: the Mughals had taken Lahore and Rohtas Fort in February 1555.

region.text: Lahore and the Punjab

ledger.note: February 1555: Lahore and the Punjab of Pakistan pass to Humayun. Sirhind page: the Mughals had taken Lahore and Rohtas Fort in February 1555; the province is my reading.

region.text: the Punjab round Sirhind

ledger.note: 22 June 1555: Sikandar Shah Suri is beaten at Sirhind. Sikandar was defeated and forced to withdraw to the Sivalik Hills in northeastern Punjab; the Indian Punjab round Sirhind is my reading of the field.

region.text: Delhi

ledger.note: 1555: the Mughals occupy Delhi. Sirhind page: they 'marched to Delhi, occupied it and reestablished their empire in India'; the page gives no month (the mughal-empire dossier has 23 July 1555); placed in June with the battle.

region.text: the Punjab from Lahore to Sirhind and the country round Delhi

ledger.note: June 1555: the fighting for the Punjab and Delhi ends with the battle of Sirhind (22 June) and the Mughal occupation of Delhi; Sikandar held out in the Sivalik Hills until he surrendered on 25 July 1557 (Sur Empire page).

region.text: Delhi and Agra

ledger.note: 7 October 1556: Hemu, Adil Shah Suri's general, takes Delhi and Agra from the Mughals. Second Panipat page: 'Hemchandra had conquered Delhi and Agra a few weeks earlier', Delhi 'after a day's battle on 7 October 1556'; he 'crowned himself Vikramaditya at Purana Quila in Delhi'.

region.text: Delhi and Agra

ledger.note: 5 November 1556: Akbar's army wins the Second Battle of Panipat and recovers Delhi and Agra. 'The Second Battle of Panipat was fought on 5 November 1556'; infobox 'Delhi and Agra captured by Akbar'.

April 1557: the last Sur emperor is killed and the state lives on as the Afghan sultanate of Bengal. Panipat page: Adil Shah was defeated and killed 'by Khizr Khan, son of Muhammad Khan Sur of Bengal, in April 1557'; the Sur Empire page lists the Muhammad Shahi dynasty of Bengal 1553-1563. Cliopatria keeps the Sur label on the eastern land; this dossier follows it.

1564: the Karrani dynasty takes Bengal. 'ruled the restored Bengal Sultanate between 1564 and 1576' (the Sur Empire page says 1563-1576); Taj Khan 'captured south-eastern Bihar and West Bengal' and then 'seized all of Bengal'.
1565: Sulaiman Khan moves the capital from Gaur to Tanda (the Karrani page has Sulaiman Khan moving it to Tanda in 1565).

region.text: Orissa as Cliopatria draws it in 1572: the coastal part (205 of Odisha's cells)

ledger.counterpart: Orissa (holder not named on the page)
ledger.note: 1568: Sulaiman Khan annexes Orissa. 'In 1568, Sulaiman Khan annexed Orissa to the Karrani sultanate permanently.' The page names the holder of Orissa in no way; Cliopatria draws the gain only from 1572.

region.text: Patna and Hajipur in Bihar, and Bengal

ledger.note: August 1574: Akbar's war for Bihar and Bengal opens at Patna. 'Akbar himself arrived at the siege carrying guns and war elephants on 3 August 1574. Hajipur followed on 6 August.' Daud Khan Karrani had nominally accepted Akbar's sovereignty under Sulaiman (Karrani page).

region.text: Patna and Hajipur

ledger.note: August 1574: Patna and Hajipur fall to the Mughals (siege of 3 August, Hajipur 6 August; the page words the fall by 'followed').

region.text: Tanda, the Karrani capital

ledger.note: 25 September 1574: the capital falls. Karrani page: 'On 25 September 1574, Munim Khan captured Tanda'; the Mughal conquest page: 'He entered the capital Tanda on 25 September 1574'.

region.text: Bengal, the country of Daud Khan Karrani

ledger.note: 10 July 1576: Rajmahal ends the war and Bengal passes to the Mughals. the decisive battle took place on 10 July 1576 (the Karrani page: 12 July); Daud was captured and executed. Daud had already submitted at Cuttack on 12 April 1575 after Tukaroi (3 March 1575), ceding Bengal and Bihar and keeping Orissa (the 'Treaty of Katak' of the Karrani page), a de jure annexation, with de facto control limited to a few towns.

region.text: Patna and Hajipur in Bihar, and Bengal

ledger.note: 10 July 1576: the war for Bihar and Bengal ends at Rajmahal.

region.text: Orissa as Cliopatria draws it from 1579: the coastal plain round Cuttack, Puri and Balasore

ledger.note: April 1592: Man Singh beats the Afghans of Orissa. Man Singh set out to conquer Odisha in April 1590; in 1591 Nasir Khan broke a treaty by besieging the Jagannath Temple at Puri; in April 1592 Man Singh fought the Afghans near the Subarnarekha River and won.

region.text: Orissa as Cliopatria draws it from 1579: the coastal plain round Cuttack, Puri and Balasore

ledger.note: 1593: Orissa is conquered. Man Singh conquered Odisha 'the following year' (after April 1592) and returned to Bihar in 1593; Ramchandra Deva of Khurda became a Mughal vassal. The mughal-empire dossier dates the Mughal gain 1595 (confidence 1, page silent); this page is nearer.

region.text: Orissa as Cliopatria draws it from 1579: the coastal plain round Cuttack, Puri and Balasore

ledger.note: 1593: the war for Orissa ends in Mughal conquest.

region.text: Orissa as Cliopatria draws it from 1579: the coastal plain round Cuttack, Puri and Balasore

ledger.note: 1593: the last land of the Sur line, Orissa, passes to the Mughal Empire after Man Singh's conquest.

wars.name: Humayun's war against Sher Shah (Gauda, Chausa, Kannauj)
wars.outcome: Sur victory: Gauda fell to Sher Shah in April 1538, Humayun seized it on 8 September 1538, the Mughals were routed at Chausa (1539) and at Kannauj on 17 May 1540, and Humayun fled to Sindh.
wars.note: Title is descriptive; the pages give the battles, not a named war.

wars.name: Sur conquest of the Punjab, Multan and Malwa
wars.outcome: Lahore taken in November 1540, Multan in 1541, Malwa annexed in 1542 with Gwalior subjugated.

wars.name: Sher Shah's Marwar campaign (Sammel)
wars.outcome: Sher Shah marched with 80,000 cavalry in early 1543; after Sammel (1544) Khawas Khan took Jodhpur and held Marwar from Ajmer to Mount Abu; Maldeo recaptured Jodhpur by July 1545 and his territories by 1546.

wars.name: Siege of Kalinjar
belligerents: Kalinjar (ruler not named on the page)
wars.outcome: Sher Shah besieged Kalinjar Fort in 1544 and was mortally wounded; he died there on 22 May 1545. The page does not give the fort's fate, so no territory is recorded.

wars.name: Islam Shah's wars with the Niazis and Gakhars
wars.outcome: Islam Shah beat the Niazis at Ambala; Haibat Khan took refuge with the Gakhars in 1548 and 'for next two years' Islam Shah 'could not defeat Gakhars or capture Haibat Khan'; the conflict with the Gakhars lasted to the end of the dynasty. No land changed hands.

wars.name: Battle of Sirhind and the Mughal reconquest of Hindustan
wars.outcome: Lahore and Rohtas fell to the Mughals in February 1555, Sikandar lost at Sirhind on 22 June 1555 and the Mughals occupied Delhi; Hemu retook Delhi and Agra on 7 October 1556 and lost them at Second Panipat on 5 November 1556.
wars.note: Second Battle of Panipat page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Battle_of_Panipat) for 1556.

wars.name: Mughal conquest of Bengal
wars.outcome: Patna and Hajipur in August 1574, Tanda on 25 September 1574, Tukaroi on 3 March 1575, Daud's submission at Cuttack on 12 April 1575 (Orissa kept), Rajmahal on 10 July 1576 and Daud's execution.
wars.note: The Karrani page dates Rajmahal 12 July 1576.

wars.name: Mughal conquest of Odisha

zones.text: Orissa as Cliopatria draws it from 1579: the coastal plain round Cuttack, Puri and Balasore

wars.outcome: Man Singh set out in April 1590, the Afghans broke a treaty at Puri in 1591, Man Singh won near the Subarnarekha in April 1592 and conquered Odisha the following year; Ramchandra Deva of Khurda became a Mughal vassal.

certainty.note: Sher Shah's empire and the Punjab, Malwa and Marwar frontiers are approximate; no page gives a surveyed boundary. Sher Shah's administration in sarkars and parganas (Sur Empire page) names units, not lines.
The sultanate of Bengal and the Afghans of Orissa have no boundary on the pages opened; the Cuttack submission of 1575 ('Treaty of Katak') cedes Bengal and Bihar by name, not by line.

sources.title: Sur Empire
sources.note: Identity, dates, rulers, Kannauj, Punjab 1540, Multan 1541, Sindh, Niazis and Gakhars, the claimants of 1554-1555, the Muhammad Shahi and Karrani successors. No area on the page.

sources.title: Sher Shah Suri
sources.note: Titles 1530-1545, Gauda April 1538, Kannauj, Malwa 1542, Marwar 1543-1544, Kalinjar 1544-1545, extent at death.

sources.title: Karrani dynasty
sources.note: 1564-1576, Gaur then Tanda 1565, Orissa 1568, Tanda 25 September 1574, Tukaroi, the Treaty of Katak, Rajmahal; no area.

sources.title: Battle of Sirhind (1555)

sources.title: Second Battle of Panipat
sources.note: Hemu in Delhi on 7 October 1556, the battle of 5 November 1556, Adil Shah's death in April 1557. A sixth page, one over the budget of five, opened because the 1556 shape lost 875,000 km2.

notes:
Cliopatria row 'Sur Empire' 1540-1594 (8 shapes, 38,835 to 1,254,263 km2). The Sur Empire page ends the empire in 1556 (Adil Shah Suri); the row goes on to 1594 with the Afghan successors in the east (Muhammad Shahi dynasty of Bengal 1553-1563, Karrani dynasty 1564-1576, the Afghans of Orissa to 1593). The sa-05-a mughal-empire dossier already names 'sur-empire' as counterpart for Patna 1574, Orissa 1575/1595 and Bengal 1576, so this dossier keeps one state from 1538 to 1593, with 'rename' events in 1557 (Muhammad Shahi dynasty) and 1564 (Karrani) and the state ending in 1593. If the orchestrator prefers a split by rule 2, the cut is 1556/1557 and the new states would be a Muhammad Shahi/Karrani Sultanate of Bengal (1553-1576, then Orissa to 1593); the 1556-1594 shapes would then be marked wrong here with the new dossier carrying them.
Start 1538 (6 April, Gauda), earlier than Cliopatria's 1540: the Hussain Shahi row (1534-1539) overlaps 1538-1539 with this dossier's new 1538 keyframe; see the hussain-shahi-dynasty dossier.
Cliopatria problems found: (1) no Punjab of Pakistan before 1547 though Lahore fell in November 1540 and Multan in 1541 (verdict adjust on the 1540 shape); (2) Malwa dropped in 1552, kept here until 1555 on the malwa-sultanate dossier's date (page not opened); (3) Bengal drawn Sur in 1553-1555 although the Muhammad Shahi dynasty is dated from 1553; (4) Orissa from 1572 against 1568; (5) Bengal drawn to 1578 against Rajmahal 1576; (6) the row ends 1594 against Man Singh's conquest in 1593; the mughal-empire dossier has Orissa passing in 1595 at confidence 1; (7) the 1547-1555 shapes hold 128 cells of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa although the Sher Shah Suri page excludes the North-West Frontier Province (left as ok: 3 percent); (8) a few Nepal and Assam cells in the Bengal and Bihar shapes.
Page silent or in conflict: Chausa is undated on the Sur page (infobox of the Sher Shah page: 1539); Rajmahal 10 July (Mughal conquest page) or 12 July 1576 (Karrani page); Karrani founded 1563 (Sur page) or 1564 (Karrani page); Sher Shah's reign starts 6 April 1538 or 17 May 1540; Multan: taken 1541 and 'later overrun by Baloch tribes' with Sher Shah assembling a campaign in 1543, not followed up; upper Sindh undated; Raisen undated on the Sur page; Kalinjar's fate unrecorded; the Sur land east of Agra (Jaunpur, Chunar) after Panipat 1556 is on no page opened; Muhammad Shahi rulers and the seat of the Orissa Afghans are on no page opened. The March 1541 revolt of Khizr Khan in Bengal (put down by Sher Shah) moved no border and is not in the ledger. Sher Shah's 'Hindustan' region (1540) is my reading; the page names no boundary.
Pages opened: 6 (budget 5): Sur Empire, Sher Shah Suri, Karrani dynasty, Battle of Sirhind (1555), Mughal conquest of Bengal, Second Battle of Panipat. No page gives an area (the Sur Empire infobox has none), so the area comparison could not be made for any shape.
Counterparts: mughal-empire (Delhi, Punjab 1540 and 1555, Delhi and Agra 1556, Patna and Tanda 1574, Bengal 1576, Orissa 1593), malwa-sultanate (1542, 1555), kingdom-of-marwar (1544-1545), sultanate-of-bengal (1538). Needing dossiers: the Muhammad Shahi dynasty / Sultanate of Bengal 1553-1576 (see above), the Gakhars (Potohar), the rulers of Multan and upper Sindh in 1541-1544 (arghun-dynasty is the likely one), the Bhoi dynasty of Orissa or whoever held Orissa in 1568.
Gazetteer: Tanda, Hajipur, Sirhind, Rohtas, Sehwan, Kalinjar and Gaur are not in the gazetteer (coordinates or a neighbouring place used).
